AAPL.rationale: Apple's fundamental health is excellent: double-digit YoY revenue (+16.6%) and EPS (+21.8%) growth, expanding gross margins (49.3% vs ~47% prior year), robust cash generation ($28.70B OCF in a seasonally weak quarter), and a rapidly strengthening balance sheet (D/E from 1.42x to 0.78x over five quarters). The Services mix shift at 70%+ gross margins and 2.5B-device installed base with ~92% retention underpin a durable franchise. However, valuation is stretched: PE at 37.4x is above the 12-month median (~35x), earnings yield of 2.7% sits 177bp below the 10-year Treasury at 4.47%, and the stock has already rallied 19.6% in the past quarter to near all-time highs ($311.23 vs $316.94 high). The recent re-rating from 31.9x to 37.4x appears to have captured much of the Q2 beat. WWDC (June 8-12) is a dated near-term catalyst — Morgan Stanley sees potential to $440 on a strong AI/Siri reveal, while UBS remains skeptical — but this is a narrative catalyst with binary outcomes, not a guaranteed fundamental re-rating. Regulatory headwinds (Supreme Court App Store ruling, EU DMA fines, DOJ suit) targeting Services economics and tariff exposure ($3.3B cumulative) add risk to the premium multiple. Net-net: a high-quality franchise with solid trajectory, but fairly valued to modestly rich at current levels, with limited margin of safety and a near-term catalyst that could go either way.
key_factors: Q2 FY2026 revenue $111.18B (+16.6% YoY), EPS $2.01 (+21.8% YoY), gross margin expanded to 49.3% from ~47% prior year
Operating cash flow $28.70B in seasonally weak quarter (+19.8% YoY); balance sheet D/E improved from 1.42x to 0.78x over five quarters
PE at 37.4x is above 12-month median (~35x) and in upper half of 30.3-43.1x range; earnings yield 2.7% vs 10-year Treasury 4.47% (177bp gap)
Stock rallied +19.6% in past quarter to $311.23, near 12-month high of $316.94 — much of Q2 beat appears priced in
WWDC 2026 (June 8-12) is imminent catalyst: Morgan Stanley target $440 on strong AI/Siri reveal, UBS skeptical; Bank of America raised PT to $380
Three-front regulatory assault: Supreme Court rejected App Store appeal (April 6), EU DMA fines, DOJ antitrust — targeting high-margin Services economics
Services revenue $96.1B in FY2025 (14% YoY growth) at ~70-77% gross margins; 2.5B installed base with ~92% retention rate
Tariff exposure: $3.3B cumulative tariffs paid; India now 25% of iPhone production, targeting majority of US-bound by end of 2026
CEO transition: Tim Cook stepping down, John Ternus named successor (April 20, 2026) — first leadership change in 15 years
$100B fresh buyback authorization and 4% dividend increase announced with Q2 earnings

sources_cited.excerpt: Morgan Stanley believes Apple's WWDC 2026 (June 8-12) could trigger a major AI narrative shift for the stock, with potential for a rally to $440… UBS remains skeptical
Apple stock rose 15% in May driven by market confidence in AI and strong iPhone sales (up 22% year-over-year)
Supreme Court rejected Apple's App Store appeal (April 6), requiring external payment links. Combined with EU DMA and DOJ suit, Apple faces a three-front regulatory battle
Services revenue grew 14% year-over-year to $96.1 billion in fiscal 2025… iPhone sales remain the cornerstone, with 231 million units sold in fiscal 2025

India now accounts for 25% of global iPhone production (up from <5% four years ago). Apple is targeting majority of US-bound iPhone production from India by end of 2026, partially offsetting the $3.3B cumulative tariff cost

$90.7 billion in share repurchases in FY2025… Apple has repurchased over $700 billion of its own stock over the past decade
